results.title: Deep-Learning Integration of CNN–Transformer and U-Net for Bi-Temporal SAR Flash-Flood Detection
results.content: deep learning; flood detection; SAR imaging; U-Net; transformer models. Remote-sensing-based flood mapping has been enriched by deep-learning techniques, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), U-Net architectures, Vision Transformers (ViTs), and hybrids that integrate these models. In contrast to transformer hybrids, which have strong demand for computation and pretraining resources [53,54] tackled this problem with the development of FET-U-Net, which includes the CNN (ResNet34) and Swin Transformer branches by high-level feature fusion and multiscale upsampling and achieved more excellent results on the task of ultrasound segmentation—a domain with imaging difficulties similar to flood detection. This innovative model features a hybrid architecture designed for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)-based flood detection, integrating U-Net’s spatial feature extraction with the Transformer’s global context modeling. At the bottleneck layer, equipped with 128 filters, the model employs three vital enhancement modules: a Compact Convolutional Transformer (CCT) tokenizer that transforms 2D pooled features into 1D tokens for sequential processing, position embedding for adding spatial awareness (a dense 128-dimensional structure), and transformer blocks that implement multihead attention mechanisms along with MLP and skip connections to capture long-range dependencies. Visual analysis reveals that CCT-U-ViT generates the most spatially coherent flood maps with excellent boundary preservation, thanks to the hierarchical feature extraction capabilities of the Compact Convolutional Transformer and the multiscale representation learning of the U-Net decoder pathway. Maps of the flood detection of the Erbil dataset using different deep-learning models (**a**) Pre-flood image; (**b**) Post-flood image; (**c**) Ground truth; (**d**) CNN 2D—1 layer; (**e**) CNN 2D—2 layer; (**f**) CNN 3D—1 layer; (**g**) CNN 3D—2 layer; (**h**) Hybrid CNN; (**i**) U-Net; (**j**) ViT; (**k**) CNN—Transformer; (**l**) CCT-U-Vit. Error distributions of the flood detection for the proposed and baseline models. This study successfully used a new hybrid deep-learning model for flood detection using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery, combining the latest advanced techniques, including CNN, U-Net, and Transformer. results.title: ResMT: A hybrid CNN-transformer framework for glioma grading with 3D MRI - ScienceDirect
results.content: # ResMT: A hybrid CNN-transformer framework for glioma grading with 3D MRI. To address these challenges, we propose ResMT, which combines CNN and transformer architectures for glioma grading, extracting both local and global features efficiently. Specifically, we designed a spatial residual module (SRM) where a 3D CNN captures glioma's volumetric complexity, and Swin UNETR, a pre-trained segmentation model, enhances the network without extra training. [17] employed a 2D-based deep learning model with transfer learning for glioma grading, using architectures such as AlexNet and GoogLeNet on a proprietary dataset, achieving a diagnostic accuracy of 0.968. In this work, we propose an attention module that effectively bridges 3D CNN and pre-trained 2D CNN models, balancing the challenges of large parameters and spatial feature learning, and incorporates a transformer block after the 2D CNN to address the limitations of CNN networks. To address these problems, we proposed a novel model that combines 3D CNN for 3D representation learning with 2D CNN for analyzing multi-plane images, alongside a transformer network to efficiently analyze the long-range relational features output by CNNs, thereby reducing computational load. Additionally, the pre-trained Swin UNETR [33] supplies crucial feature information for tumor segmentation, and the spatial residual attention module directs the model to enhance focus on tumor areas, eliminates the need for the extensive, time-consuming extraction of numerous handcrafted features typical of radiomics methods. We introduce a novel model ResMT seamlessly integrates 3D CNN, 2D CNN and transformer for glioma grading. We efficiently combined pre-trained Swin UNETR and 3D CNN architectures for glioma grading using Spatial Residual learning feature extraction. Consequently, our ResMT outperforms methods that solely use 2D or 3D CNN networks, improving performance and accuracy in glioma grading. Our proposed model, ResMT, integrates various deep learning components, including the 3D spatial residual attention module, channel attention block, and transformer networks, as shown in Fig. 1. ### Deep multi-scale 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) for MRI gliomas brain tumor classification. This study explores the potential of deep learning to overcome these limitations, proposing a novel hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN) approach in classifying low-grade (LGG) and high-grade (HGG) tumors on T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (T2-W MRI) data.

results.content: # Review — CoTr: Efficiently Bridging CNN and Transformer for 3D Medical Image Segmentation. ## CoTr, Deformable Transformer Used In Between Encoder & Decoder. > **CoTr: Efficiently Bridging CNN and Transformer for 3D Medical Image Segmentation**,. * **Convolutional neural network and a** **Transformer** **(CoTr)** is proposed, where the **CNN** is constructed to **extract feature representations** and an efficient **deformable** **Transformer** **(DeTrans)** is built to **model the long-range dependency** on the extracted feature maps. * **(c)** **TransUNet** **and (d) CoTr** encoders are both the hybrid of CNN and Transformer. * The CNN-encoder, ***FCNN*(·)** contains a **Conv-IN-****LeakyReLU** **block** and **three stages of 3D residual blocks**. > Given an input image *x* with a height of *H*, a width of *W*, and a depth (i.e., number of slices) of *D*, **the** **feature maps produced by *FCNN*(·)** can be formally expressed as:. * The CNN-encoder cannot capture the long-range dependency of pixels effectively, **DeTrans-encoder** is used to introduce the **multi-scale deformable self-attention (MS-DMSA)** mechanism for efficient **long-range contextual modeling**. * The DeTrans-encoder is a composition of **an input-to-sequence layer** and ***LD* stacked deformable** **Transformer** **(DeTrans) layers**. > For each feature level *l*, ***PED*, *PEH*, and *PEW*** are **concatenated** as the **3D positional encoding *pl*** and **combine it with the flattened *fl* via element-wise summation** to form the input sequence of DeTrans-encoder. * In **CoTr∗**, there is **only one 3D residual block in each stage of CNN-encoder**. * In **CoTr†**, the **number of 3D residual blocks in each stage** of CNN-encoder is **two**. * Third, **CoTr∗** **with comparable parameters** **significantly outperforms ‘CoTr w/o CNN-encoder’**, improving the average Dice over 11 organs by 4%. > It suggests that the **hybrid CNN-****Transformer** **encoder** has **distinct advantages over the pure** **Transformer** **encoder** in medical image segmentation. * The original **2D** **TransUNet**is **extended** to a **3D** version by using 3D CNN-encoder and decoder is as done in CoTr. * **(a-c)**: In the DeTrans-encoder, there are **three hyper-parameters, i.e., *K*, *H*, and *LD***, which represent the **number of sampled key points, heads, and stacked DeTrans layers**, respectively. * **(d)**: To demonstrate the performance gain resulted from the multi-scale strategy, it is also attempted to train **CoTr with single-scale feature maps from the last stage**.

If you want to convert or extract video frames from scratch, here are some nice tutorials: ## Models ### 1. 3D CNN (train from scratch) Use several 3D kernels of size *(a,b,c)* and channels *n*, *e.g., (a, b, c, n) = (3, 3, 3, 16)* to convolve with video input, where videos are viewed as 3D images. The CRNN model is a pair of CNN encoder and RNN decoder (see figure below): * **[encoder]** A CNN function encodes (meaning compressing dimension) every 2D image **x(t)** into a 1D vector **z(t)** by * **[decoder]** A RNN receives a sequence input vectors **z(t)** from the CNN encoder and outputs another 1D sequence **h(t)**. * In the test phase, the models are almost the same as the training phase, except that dropout has to be removed and batchnorm layer uses moving average and variance instead of mini-batch values. *eg.,* for 3D-CNN model * `UCF101_3DCNN.py`: model parameters, training/testing process.
